```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)

#course data (read once for the whole page)

  st_transform(2264)
pm <- st_read("https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1zf1xk-7pOoSnEwGvGsNVa6XejFoPFzdJ", quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_transform(2264)
schools <- st_read("https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1i-C2PF3ajbpHTlavh3m1QbWNObpobprZ", quiet = TRUE)
schools <- schools |> filter(!duplicated(st_coordinates(schools)))

#numbers quoted in the text below come from here, so they stay right if the data changes
fmt <- function(x, d = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")
lisa_colors <- c("High-High" = "#B2182B", "Low-Low" = "#2166AC", "High-Low" = "#F4A582",
                 "Low-High" = "#92C5DE", "Not significant" = "#E5E5E5")
```

This tutorial runs over two class days. Day 1 covers neighbors and global Moran's I, and Day 2 covers local Moran's I (LISA). Each day has its own walkthrough, partner practice and index card.

## Day 1 Walkthrough: Global Moran's I {#walkthrough}

Run each chunk in your own .Rmd. You will reuse this code in the Day 1 partner practice.

### Step 1: Load and Map the Data

::: {.why}
We'll use `pct_pov`, the percent of people below the poverty line, for North Carolina's 100 counties from the 2019 to 2023 [American Community Survey](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs.html). Spatial autocorrelation asks whether nearby places have similar values.
:::

```{r, eval = FALSE}
#load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(spdep)
library(tmap)

#NC counties, projected to NC State Plane (feet)
nc_counties <- st_read("https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1hXVtKL_33c4QRw6_Z9LlYqjgisdYCRqX") |>
  st_transform(2264)
```

```{r, fig.alt = "Map of percent of people in poverty by North Carolina county in five quantile classes, with a legend. The highest poverty rates are in the northeast and in Robeson and nearby counties in the southeast, and the lowest are around Charlotte, Raleigh and the mountains near Asheville."}
tm_shape(nc_counties) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "pct_pov",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(style = "quantile", n = 5, values = "brewer.or_rd"),
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "People in poverty (%)"))
```

### Step 2: Define Neighbors

::: {.why}
Moran's I needs a definition of who counts as a neighbor. Queen contiguity makes two counties neighbors if they share any border or corner. For points, k-nearest neighbors makes each point's k closest points its neighbors.
:::

```{r, fig.alt = "Map of North Carolina county outlines with a line connecting the center of each county to the center of every county that shares a border or corner with it."}
#queen contiguity
county_nb <- poly2nb(nc_counties, queen = TRUE)
summary(county_nb)

#draw the links between neighbors
plot(st_geometry(nc_counties), border = "grey")
plot(county_nb, st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_geometry(nc_counties))), add = TRUE, col = "black")

#for points, k-nearest neighbors (here k = 6) would look like this:
#knn2nb(knearneigh(points_sf, k = 6))
```

### Step 3: Weights and Moran's I

::: {.why}
`nb2listw()` turns neighbors into weights. `style = "W"` gives each county's neighbors weights that add to 1. `moran.mc()` compares the observed Moran's I with 999 random shuffles of the values. I near 0 means no autocorrelation, positive means similar values are near each other, and negative means unlike values are near each other.
:::

```{r}
county_w <- nb2listw(county_nb, style = "W")

set.seed(391)
moran.mc(nc_counties$pct_pov, county_w, nsim = 999)
```

### Step 4: Moran Scatterplot

::: {.why}
The scatterplot puts each county's value on the x-axis and the average of its neighbors (the spatial lag) on the y-axis. The slope of the line is Moran's I.
:::

```{r, fig.alt = "Moran scatterplot of county poverty rate against the average poverty rate of neighboring counties. The points slope upward from lower left to upper right, showing positive spatial autocorrelation."}
moran.plot(nc_counties$pct_pov, county_w,
           xlab = "People in poverty (%)", ylab = "Neighbors' average (%)")
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
set.seed(391)
pov_moran <- moran.mc(nc_counties$pct_pov, nb2listw(poly2nb(nc_counties)), nsim = 999)
```

Moran's I is `r fmt(pov_moran$statistic)` with a p-value of `r fmt(pov_moran$p.value, 3)`, so high-poverty counties tend to sit near other high-poverty counties.

## Day 1 Partner Practice {#partner-practice}

Partner A uses mean PM2.5 (µg/m³) from 2016 to 2020 for `r fmt(nrow(pm), 0)` North Carolina census tracts, from the [CDC Environmental Public Health Tracking Network](https://ephtracking.cdc.gov/). Partner B uses `avg_sat_score` for `r nrow(schools)` North Carolina public high schools. Each task tells you in parentheses which walkthrough step to reuse.

```{r, eval = FALSE}

pm <- st_read("https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1zf1xk-7pOoSnEwGvGsNVa6XejFoPFzdJ") |>

schools <- st_read("https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1i-C2PF3ajbpHTlavh3m1QbWNObpobprZ")
schools <- schools |> filter(!duplicated(st_coordinates(schools)))
```

## Day 2 Walkthrough: Local Moran's I (LISA) {#walkthrough-2}

Use the county data, neighbors and weights from Day 1.

### Step 1: Local Moran's I

::: {.why}
Global Moran's I gives one number for the whole map. Local Moran's I gives one for each county and tests it against 999 random shuffles. `localmoran_perm()` returns a matrix, and its `quadr` attribute says which quadrant of the Moran scatterplot each county falls in.
:::

```{r}
set.seed(391)
county_lisa <- localmoran_perm(nc_counties$pct_pov, county_w, nsim = 999)
head(county_lisa)
```

### Step 2: Classify the Clusters

::: {.why}
A county is High-High if it is high and its neighbors are high, and Low-Low if both are low. High-Low and Low-High are outliers. Counties with a p-value of 0.05 or more are labeled not significant.
:::

```{r}
nc_counties <- nc_counties |>
  mutate(lisa_p = county_lisa[, "Pr(z != E(Ii)) Sim"],
         lisa_quad = as.character(attr(county_lisa, "quadr")$mean),
         lisa_cluster = ifelse(lisa_p < 0.05, lisa_quad, "Not significant"))

table(nc_counties$lisa_cluster)
```

### Step 3: Map the Clusters

::: {.why}
Give each cluster type a fixed color, and keep the legend so the map can be read without relying on color alone.
:::

```{r, fig.alt = "LISA cluster map of county poverty rates with a legend. A High-High cluster of high poverty covers counties in the northeast, such as Bertie, Northampton, Martin, Edgecombe and Pitt, and in the southeast around Robeson, Hoke and Scotland. A Low-Low cluster covers Mecklenburg, Cabarrus and Iredell. Most counties are not significant."}
lisa_colors <- c("High-High" = "#B2182B", "Low-Low" = "#2166AC", "High-Low" = "#F4A582",
                 "Low-High" = "#92C5DE", "Not significant" = "#E5E5E5")

tm_shape(nc_counties) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "lisa_cluster",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = lisa_colors),
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "LISA cluster"))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
set.seed(391)
k_lisa <- localmoran_perm(nc_counties$pct_pov, nb2listw(poly2nb(nc_counties)), nsim = 999)
k_clus <- ifelse(k_lisa[, "Pr(z != E(Ii)) Sim"] < 0.05, as.character(attr(k_lisa, "quadr")$mean), "Not significant")
```

`r sum(k_clus == "High-High")` counties are High-High and `r sum(k_clus == "Low-Low")` are Low-Low. The other `r sum(!k_clus %in% c("High-High", "Low-Low"))` are outliers or not significant.

## Answer Key {#answer-key .answer-key}

```{r key-values, include = FALSE}
pm_w <- nb2listw(poly2nb(pm, queen = TRUE), style = "W", zero.policy = TRUE)
sch_w <- nb2listw(knn2nb(knearneigh(schools, k = 6)), style = "W")
set.seed(391); pm_m <- moran.mc(pm$meanpm_2016_2020, pm_w, nsim = 999, zero.policy = TRUE)
set.seed(391); sch_m <- moran.mc(schools$avg_sat_score, sch_w, nsim = 999)
classify <- function(l) ifelse(l[, "Pr(z != E(Ii)) Sim"] < 0.05, as.character(attr(l, "quadr")$mean), "Not significant")
set.seed(391); pm_c <- classify(localmoran_perm(pm$meanpm_2016_2020, pm_w, nsim = 999, zero.policy = TRUE))
set.seed(391); sch_c <- classify(localmoran_perm(schools$avg_sat_score, sch_w, nsim = 999))
cnt <- function(cl, k) sum(cl == k)
types <- c("High-High", "Low-Low", "High-Low", "Low-High", "Not significant")
row_txt <- function(cl) paste(sapply(types, function(k) fmt(cnt(cl, k), 0)), collapse = " | ")
```

### Day 1

| Variable | Neighbors | Moran's I | p-value |
|---|---|---|---|
| PM2.5 in tracts | Queen contiguity | `r fmt(pm_m$statistic)` | `r fmt(pm_m$p.value, 3)` |
| SAT scores at schools | 6 nearest | `r fmt(sch_m$statistic)` | `r fmt(sch_m$p.value, 3)` |

A p-value of 0.001 is the smallest possible with 999 shuffles. PM2.5 is far more strongly autocorrelated: its scatterplot points hug a steep line, while the SAT scatterplot is a loose cloud with a gentle slope. PM2.5 comes from air that moves across tract borders and from regional sources, so neighboring tracts share it almost by definition. SAT scores depend on each school's students and programs, and neighboring schools can be very different, for example a magnet or early college next to a traditional high school.

### Day 2

| Variable | High-High | Low-Low | High-Low | Low-High | Not significant |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PM2.5 in tracts | `r row_txt(pm_c)` |
| SAT scores at schools | `r row_txt(sch_c)` |

Because these are permutation tests, counts can differ by a few with another seed or R version. About `r round(100 * mean(pm_c != "Not significant"))`% of tracts are in a significant cluster, compared with `r round(100 * mean(sch_c != "Not significant"))`% of schools, which matches the much larger global Moran's I for PM2.5. PM2.5 High-High tracts run through the Piedmont urban crescent from Charlotte through the Triad to the Triangle, and Low-Low tracts are in the mountains and along the coast. SAT High-High schools are around Chapel Hill, Cary and Raleigh and around Asheville, and Low-Low schools include parts of Charlotte, Winston-Salem and the rural northeast and southeast.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
#### Day 1, Partner A: PM2.5 ####
pm <- st_read("https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1zf1xk-7pOoSnEwGvGsNVa6XejFoPFzdJ") |>
  st_transform(2264)

tm_shape(pm) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "meanpm_2016_2020", col_alpha = 0,
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(style = "quantile", n = 5, values = "brewer.or_rd"),
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Mean PM2.5 (µg/m³)"))

pm_nb <- poly2nb(pm, queen = TRUE)
pm_w <- nb2listw(pm_nb, style = "W", zero.policy = TRUE)
set.seed(391)
moran.mc(pm$meanpm_2016_2020, pm_w, nsim = 999, zero.policy = TRUE)
moran.plot(pm$meanpm_2016_2020, pm_w, zero.policy = TRUE)

#### Day 1, Partner B: SAT scores ####
schools <- st_read("https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1i-C2PF3ajbpHTlavh3m1QbWNObpobprZ")
schools <- schools |> filter(!duplicated(st_coordinates(schools)))

tm_shape(schools) +
  tm_dots(fill = "avg_sat_score", size = 0.5,
          fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(style = "quantile", n = 5, values = "brewer.or_rd"),
          fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Average SAT score"))

sch_nb <- knn2nb(knearneigh(schools, k = 6))
sch_w <- nb2listw(sch_nb, style = "W")
set.seed(391)
moran.mc(schools$avg_sat_score, sch_w, nsim = 999)
moran.plot(schools$avg_sat_score, sch_w)

#### Day 2, Partner A: PM2.5 clusters ####
set.seed(391)
pm_lisa <- localmoran_perm(pm$meanpm_2016_2020, pm_w, nsim = 999, zero.policy = TRUE)
pm <- pm |>
  mutate(lisa_p = pm_lisa[, "Pr(z != E(Ii)) Sim"],
         lisa_quad = as.character(attr(pm_lisa, "quadr")$mean),
         lisa_cluster = ifelse(lisa_p < 0.05, lisa_quad, "Not significant"))
table(pm$lisa_cluster)

tm_shape(pm) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "lisa_cluster", col_alpha = 0,
              fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = lisa_colors),
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "LISA cluster"))

#### Day 2, Partner B: SAT clusters ####
set.seed(391)
sch_lisa <- localmoran_perm(schools$avg_sat_score, sch_w, nsim = 999)
schools <- schools |>
  mutate(lisa_p = sch_lisa[, "Pr(z != E(Ii)) Sim"],
         lisa_quad = as.character(attr(sch_lisa, "quadr")$mean),
         lisa_cluster = ifelse(lisa_p < 0.05, lisa_quad, "Not significant"))
table(schools$lisa_cluster)

tm_shape(schools) +
  tm_dots(fill = "lisa_cluster", size = 0.5,
          fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = lisa_colors),
          fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "LISA cluster"))
```
